SWEEP 3 SLICE TWO LANDED b0831b1: features measured, MIRROR DOOR OPEN ON 4 OF 4.

RUNNING TOTAL: 25 OF 25 MEASURED ARE FORGEABLE. view 21/21 (c5a119a), features 4/4 (b0831b1). No
exceptions, which is what the mechanism predicts -- `case class X private` derives Mirror.ProductOf
regardless of module, so the SHAPE is what matters and not where it lives.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THE BEAD'S OWN FRAMING: I filed sweep 3 saying "learn how many are actually
forgeable rather than assuming all 38". The honest read of 25 consecutive positives is that the
remaining 13 will behave the same way, and the measurement's value has shifted -- it is no longer
suspense about the count, it is A DURABLE RECORD THAT FAILS WHEN SOMEONE FIXES ONE. Both slices pin
the known-bad state and fail loudly on closure, asking for the name to be removed.

REMAINING: 13 across core, codec and align. I am NOT measuring align tonight -- scout's and m1's
candidates live there and adding tests would change align's count and invalidate their gate
evidence. core and codec are free of pending candidates and are the natural next slices.

Both slices carry a positive control for the SUMMON door specifically, and I ran the mutation on
each rather than describing it: point one entry at core.SurfaceAtlas, proven sealed earlier
tonight, and confirm the test fails. Reverted and grep-verified both times.

CostBreakdown remains slice one by exposure rather than convenience -- it is the only member of the
population carrying a live wire guarantee with a demonstrated forge -- but it is in align and waits
for batch 1 to clear.
